answer: A harbor master gives each agent one tide pole on its own knoll above the harbor, with a thin onyx band set into the wood at the high-water mark. Each dawn the keeper reads the waterline against the band and carves the number into the pole, and at dusk a second keeper re-reads the band and checks the carving. A pole with a rubbed carving or a reading that misses the tide table loses its mooring for a month. A thousand fake names need a thousand poles on a thousand knolls and a thousand dawn readings, and no copy can stand on a knoll already taken.
